## TASK 1 — Corner-collapse root cause

**Root cause: `g_paint_vp_w/h/x/y` are single module-global viewport dims, written unconditionally by EVERY `drawScene`, so in the embedded editor the mesh-edit pane's viewport gets clobbered by an unrelated Scene3D (a library thumbnail tile).**

The chain, file:line:

1. **The globals are shared, one-per-process.** `framework/gpu/3d.zig:429-438` declares `g_paint_vp_w/h/x/y` as module vars. Every overlay projection and every pick reads them: `drawEditorOverlay` at `3d.zig:1223/1237/1238` (`model_paint.project(cam, g_paint_vp_w, g_paint_vp_h, …)`), face pick at `1280`, marquee at `1248`, gizmo at `1057-1135`, focus at `418`.

2. **They are written unconditionally at the end of `drawScene`** — `3d.zig:3729-3732` (`g_paint_vp_w = w; g_paint_vp_h = h; g_paint_vp_x = vp_x; g_paint_vp_y = vp_y;`). The comment two lines up (`3d.zig:3725`) literally says *"Only meaningful when this scene holds the paint target"* — but **the gate was documented and never implemented.** Every scene overwrites them.

3. **`drawScene` runs once per Scene3D per frame, in tree order**, via `flushPending` → `for (g_pending…) |p| drawScene(…)` at `3d.zig:3187`. Whatever Scene3D is drawn **last** leaves its `w/h/x/y` in the globals.

4. **The embedded editor paints many Scene3D nodes**, not one. `cart/editor/library/ModelThumbnail.tsx:23` renders a `<Scene3D>` per model tile in the library/content browser (small, ~tile-sized, its own origin), alongside the single ModelView pane (`cart/editor/stage/ModelDocumentSurface.tsx:43-44`, `cart/modelview.tsx:585`). Standalone OBJ import has exactly **one** Scene3D filling the window, so the globals always describe the mesh-edit viewport → correct.

5. **`drawEditorOverlay` reads the globals at the wrong time relative to the writer.** It is called during the paint walk (`framework/engine.zig:3176`, right after `r3d.render()` which only *records* into `g_pending` and defers the actual draw). So at overlay-emit time the globals still hold the **previous frame's last drawScene** — a thumbnail's dims/origin. Picks (`meshEditPickFace`, run during input between frames) read the same last-writer value. Both therefore use a thumbnail's viewport.

6. **Why it collapses to the top-left specifically:** `model_paint.project` (`framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:318-330`) returns viewport-**local** coords `((ndc_x*0.5+0.5)*vp_w, (1-ndc_y)*0.5*vp_h)`, i.e. spread across `0..vp_w × 0..vp_h`, which `drawEditorOverlay` then offsets by `+ox,+oy = r.x,r.y` (the pane origin). With `vp_w/vp_h` holding a small thumbnail size, the whole model's NDC range gets scaled into a tiny (thumbnail-sized) cluster, dumped at the pane's top-left origin — exactly the "handles piled in the top-left corner" symptom. Face picking fails for the same reason: `model_paint.pick(cam, g_paint_vp_w, g_paint_vp_h, vpLocalX(mx), vpLocalY(my))` at `3d.zig:1280` builds the ray with the wrong viewport (and wrong `vp_x/vp_y` offset), so the ray misses the mesh.

**Recommended minimal fix:** Gate the capture at `3d.zig:3726-3732` so it only writes when *this* scene holds the mesh-edit/paint target — implement the gate the comment already promises. `drawScene` already has the exact test it needs: it checks `model_paint.isTarget(hashKey(gk))` per child mesh at `3d.zig:4121` (`model_paint.isTarget` / `model_source` key hash `g_key_hash`). Pre-scan the scene's children for a `child.scene3d_geom_key` whose `hashKey` is `model_paint.isTarget(...)` (thumbnails use generated `geometry=` defs, not the target `hostKey`, so they never match), set a `scene_holds_target` bool before line 3726, and only write `g_paint_eye/target/fov/vp_w/vp_h/vp_x/vp_y` when true. That makes the target scene the sole writer, so the globals always describe the mesh-edit viewport regardless of paint order — fixing both the overlay collapse and the face-pick miss. (This also finally scopes the overlay to the correct viewport, which the `engine.zig:3173-3174` `EDITOR_OVERLAY_MIN_PANE` size-heuristic was a stopgap for.)

## TASK 2 — Fix B (n-gon face grouping) feasibility

**Existing `face_to_source` CANNOT be reused for n-gon grouping — it maps to source *triangles*, not original polygons. New plumbing is required.**

- The map **is** retained and reachable at edit time: `mesh_import.decimateExpanded` returns `DecimatedMesh.face_to_source` (`mesh_import.zig:680-687, 774-777`), stored via `model_source.setFaceMap` (`v8_bindings_core.zig:802`) into `model_source.g_face_to_source` (`model_source.zig:16`), and used live by `writeColor`/`updateGeometryFromDisplayed`. So a displayed-face → source-face lookup exists during editing.

- **But "source face" = a source *triangle*, not the original OBJ n-gon.** `g_source_verts` is expanded soup (8 f32/vert, 3 verts/tri), and `face_to_source[displayed] = source-triangle-index`. The map only bridges the *decimation* level (displayed tri → pre-decimation tri).

- **The original 34-n-gon identity is destroyed earlier, at triangulation, and never recorded.** The OBJ face parser (`mesh_import.zig:655-662`) fan-triangulates each `f` polygon into N-2 anonymous `b.triangle()` calls with **no polygon-id tag**. Nothing downstream carries which OBJ polygon a triangle came from. So the data to group triangles back into the 34 faces is **not present anywhere in the host**.

- **What Fix B needs (new plumbing):**
  1. During OBJ parse, increment a polygon counter per `f` statement and emit a parallel per-triangle `source_polygon: []u32` array (tag each fan triangle with its polygon id). (GLB has no n-gons — every primitive triangle is its own "polygon"; this is OBJ-specific.)
  2. Compose it through `decimateExpanded` (displayed-tri → source-tri → source-polygon) and store the source-tri→polygon array in `model_source` alongside `g_face_to_source`.
  3. Expose grouping to `mesh_edit` so face selection selects all triangles sharing a polygon id, and have `drawEditorOverlay` (edge mode) draw the n-gon's boundary edges rather than per-triangle edges.

  (A heuristic coplanar-adjacent-triangle merge could approximate grouping without parse-time ids, but it would not reproduce the authoritative 34 faces and can mis-merge coplanar neighbors — the parse-time polygon index is the correct source of truth.)

**Files that matter:** `framework/gpu/3d.zig` (globals `429-438`, capture `3726-3732`, overlay `1199-1243`, target test `4121`), `framework/engine.zig:3164-3178`, `framework/gpu/model_paint.zig:318-330`, `framework/world/mesh_import.zig:625-663 / 680-778`, `framework/gpu/model_source.zig`, `framework/v8_bindings_core.zig:766-802`, `cart/editor/library/ModelThumbnail.tsx:23`.</result>
